newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis Convention Authority issue BBB - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis Convention Authority issue BBB - Fitch.

text.p: The St. Louis Regional Convention and Sports Complex Authority (MO.)'s approximately $60,000,000 convention and sports facility project and refunding bonds, series C 1997 (The City of St. Louis, Sponsor), payable from annually renewable lease payments to be made by the city, are rated 'BBB' by Fitch Investors Service.
Additionally, the authority's outstanding $8,820,000 convention and sports facility project bonds, series C 1991, are affirmed at 'BBB' and the city's outstanding general obligation rating at 'BBB+'.
Series C 1997 bonds are scheduled to be sold through negotiation the week of Feb. 17 via a syndicate led by Smith Barney, Inc.

The bonds are being issued to advance refund $47.2 million of the authority's outstanding series C 1991 bonds, pay the costs of series 1997 project additions and pay costs of issuance. Series C 1991 bonds, together with series A 1991 (State of Missouri, Sponsor) and series B 1991 (St. Louis County, MO., Sponsor) were issued to finance the eastern expansion of the A.J. Cervantes Convention Center (the Trans World Dome) located in St. Louis. Series C 1997 bonds are limited obligations of the authority, payable solely from annual appropriations from the city.

The ratings reflect the credit characteristics of St. Louis, as sponsor, under the financing agreement. While the city has experienced a long-term decline in population and manufacturing employment, its downtown remains a viable business/service center concentrated around health, education, convention and entertainment enterprises.

The city has maintained a history of positive financial operations and reserves. General fund revenue sources are heavily weighted toward taxing business and commercial activity in the city, capturing regional wealth while offsetting marginal taxable property growth.
Imposition of a 1/2% sales tax in 1993 dedicated for capital improvements has enabled the city to begin addressing deferred maintenance and capital spending.
